_meta.role: Software Engineer Hardware Diagnostics New Grad

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, working at the boundary of systems software and physical hardware. Writes bare-metal C driver code on Cortex-M4 for GPIO, timers, ADC, and I2C, works from schematics and datasheets through PCB fabrication to board bring-up, and builds Python and C tooling to stress and verify hardware performance.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a cross-functional 25-member robotics team across national competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Architected a metal surface inspection pipeline for microscopic crack analysis using custom image stitching, wavelet denoising, and depth estimation.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Built a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to emit HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver on Cortex-M4.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret (Jetson + STM32)
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing over I2C.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 hardware/software integration failures including servo brown-out and stale-frame capture; achieved 100% pick reliability across 10/10 trials.
Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms) for visual servoing and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via a TCA9548A I2C mux.

projects.name: MPI Hodgkin-Huxley Neuron Simulation
bullets: Implemented distributed dendrite computations across MPI workers with synchronous soma updates on a SLURM-managed cluster.
